## Passages
RESULT [curation]: Combining multiple sources 'does not necessarily yield better models, but rather dilutes the robustness of the best individual data source'.
US [curation]: This is direct evidence for the professor's per-increment check. A harvested source can make the merged model WORSE even when it is clean, simply by diluting the best source. Increments should therefore be source-attributed and measured one source (or cluster) at a time against the sealed holdout, with rollback at source granularity.
CORRECTION [curation]: NeurIPS 2022 oral confirmed, with the same six sources. The quote 'does not necessarily yield better models, but rather dilutes the robustness of the best individual data source' is verbatim.
